65:1: Interpretation of Surat At-Talaq In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was first addressed as an honor and a sign of respect, then he addressed the nation as a consequence, saying: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Thawaab ibn Sa’id al-Hibari told us, Asbat ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced Hafsa, and she went to her family, so God revealed: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them for their prescribed waiting period. It was said to him: Take her back, for she is a woman who fasts and prays, and she is one of your wives and women in Paradise. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Bashar, on the authority of Abd al-A’la, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, and he mentioned it as a mursal. It has been reported from more than one source that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced Hafsa and then took her back. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya bin Bakir told us, Al-Layth told us, Aqeel told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Salim told me that Abdullah bin Umar told him that he divorced his wife while she was menstruating. Umar mentioned this to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became angry and said: “Let him take her back, then keep her until she is pure, then menstruates and then becomes pure. If he wants to divorce her, let him divorce her while she is pure before having intercourse with her. That is the waiting period that God, the Almighty, has commanded.” This is how Al-Bukhari narrated it here. He narrated it in other places in his book and in Muslim, and his wording is: That is the waiting period that God has commanded that women be divorced. The authors of books and Musnads narrated it through various chains of transmission and with many wordings. The place to fully discuss it is in the books of rulings. The most recent wording to be mentioned here is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih through Ibn Jurayj: Abu Al-Zubayr told me that he heard Abd Al-Rahman bin Ayman, the freed slave of Uzza, asking Ibn Umar, while Abu Al-Zubayr was listening: What do you think of a man who divorces his wife while she is menstruating? He said: Ibn Omar divorced his wife while she was menstruating during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let him take her back. He returned her and said: When she becomes pure, let him divorce her or keep her. Ibn Umar said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them during their prescribed waiting period. Al-A’mash narrated from Malik ibn al-Harith from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid from Abdullah, regarding the verse: divorce them during their prescribed waiting period, he said: The period of purity without intercourse. A similar narration was narrated from Ibn Umar, Ata’, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, Maymun ibn Mihran, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. It is also a narration from Ikrimah and al-Dahhak. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: divorce them during their prescribed waiting period, he said: He should not divorce her while she is menstruating or during a period of purity in which he has had intercourse with her, but he should leave her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he can divorce her once. Ikrimah said: divorce them during their prescribed waiting period, the waiting period is purity and the menstrual period. If a man divorces a pregnant woman while it is clear that she is pregnant, but he has had intercourse with her, he does not know whether she is pregnant or not. From here, the jurists took the rulings of divorce and divided it into sunnah divorce and heretical divorce. Sunnah divorce is when he divorces her while she is pure and has not had intercourse with her, or when she is pregnant and her pregnancy has become clear. Heretic divorce is when he divorces her during her menstruation, or during a period of purity in which he has had intercourse with her and he does not know whether she is pregnant or not. There is a third divorce in which there is neither sunnah nor heretical divorce, which is the divorce of a young girl, a woman who has despaired of marriage, or one who has not been consummated with. The explanation of this and what is related to it is fully explained in the books of branches of knowledge, and God Almighty knows best. God the Almighty says: And count the waiting period meaning, memorize it and know its beginning and end, so that the waiting period does not become too long for the woman and she is prevented from having husbands. And fear God, your Lord meaning in that. God the Almighty says: Do not turn them out of their houses, nor should they leave meaning, during the waiting period, she has the right to reside with the husband as long as she is observing her waiting period from him. The man does not have the right to turn her out, nor is it permissible for her to leave because she is also detained by the husband’s right. God the Almighty says: {Unless they commit a clear immorality} meaning that they should not leave their homes unless the woman commits a clear immorality, in which case she leaves the house. Clear immorality includes adultery, as stated by Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn `Abbas, Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Sha`bi, al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Mujahid, `Ikrimah, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qilabah, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak, Zayd ibn Aslam, `Ata` al-Khurasani, al-Suddi, Sa`id ibn Abi Hilal, and others. It also includes if a woman rebels or speaks insolently toward a man’s family and hurts them in words or actions, as stated by Ubayy ibn Ka`b, Ibn `Abbas, `Ikrimah, and others. God the Almighty says: {And these are the limits set by God} meaning His laws and prohibitions. {And whoever transgresses the limits set by God} meaning he goes beyond them and transgresses them to something else and does not obey them, {has wronged himself}, meaning by doing that. And the Almighty said: You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that something new. That is, We only kept the divorced woman in the husband’s house during the waiting period so that the husband might regret divorcing her and God Almighty would create in his heart the desire to take her back, so that it would be easier and simpler. Al-Zuhri said on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah on the authority of Fatimah bint Qays regarding the Almighty’s saying: You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that something new. She said: It is the return. And this is what Al-Sha’bi, Ata’, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Ath-Thawri said. And from here, those of the Salaf and those who followed them, such as Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God have mercy on them, went to the view that housing is not obligatory for the woman whose divorce has been severed, and likewise for the woman whose husband has died. They also relied on the hadith of Fatimah bint Qays Al-Fihriyyah when her husband Abu Amr ibn Hafs divorced her with the last of three divorces, and he was absent from her in Yemen, so he sent her that, and his agent sent her barley, meaning maintenance, but she was displeased with him, so he said: By God, you do not have maintenance from us. So she went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said: You have no right to maintenance from him, and to Muslim: nor residence. And he ordered her to observe her waiting period in the house of Umm Sharik. Then he said: “That is a woman whom my companions visit. Perform your waiting period at the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man. You should take off your clothes.” The hadith. Imam Ahmad narrated it from another chain of transmission with a different wording. He said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, Mujalid told us, Aamer told us: I came to Madinah and went to Fatimah bint Qais, and she told me that her husband divorced her during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him on a military expedition. She said: His brother said to me: Go out of the house. I said: I have maintenance and housing until the time comes. He said: No. She said: So I went to the Messenger of God and said: So-and-so divorced me and his brother expelled me and prevented me from housing and maintenance. He said to him: What do you have to do with the daughter of the family of Qais? He said: O Messenger of God, my brother divorced her three times at once. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Look, O daughter of the family of Qais, the maintenance and housing of a woman are due from her husband as long as he has the right to take her back. If he has not the right to take her back, then she has no maintenance or housing. Go out and stay with so-and-so.” Then he said that he was speaking to her: Go to Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is blind and cannot see you. And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Bazzar al-Tastari told us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Sawaaf told us, Bakr ibn Bakkar told us, Saeed ibn Yazid al-Bajali told us, Aamer al-Shaabi told us that he entered upon Fatimah bint Qays, the sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays al-Qurashi, and her husband Abu Amr ibn Hafs ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, and she said: Abu Amr ibn Hafs sent me a message while he was setting out with an army to Yemen, asking for my divorce. I asked his guardians about my maintenance and housing, but they said: He did not send us anything about that, nor did he command us about it. So I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, Abu Amr ibn Hafs sent me a message about my divorce, so I asked my guardians about my housing and maintenance, but his guardians said: He did not send us anything about that. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Housing and maintenance are only for the woman if her husband has the right to take her back. If she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband, then she is not entitled to maintenance or housing.” And this is how al-Nasa’i narrated it from Ahmad. Ibn Yahya Al-Sufi, on the authority of Abu Naim Al-Fadl Ibn Dakin, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Yazid, who is Al-Ahmasi Al-Bajali Al-Kufi. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He is a sheikh who narrates from him.
65:2: God Almighty says: “And when the women in waiting have reached their term, meaning they are close to the end of their waiting period but the waiting period has not been completed completely, then at that time either the husband decides to keep her, which is to return her to the protection of his marriage and to continue with her as she was with him “with kindness,” meaning treating her well in his company, or he decides to separate from her with kindness, meaning without quarreling, insulting, or being harsh, but rather he divorces her in a beautiful way and in a good manner. God the Almighty said: And bring to witness two just men from among you meaning, regarding taking her back if you decide on it, as narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah on the authority of Imran bin Husayn that he was asked about a man who divorces a woman and then has intercourse with her without witnessing her divorce or taking her back, so he said: She was divorced for a reason other than the Sunnah and she took her back for a reason other than the Sunnah, and I bear witness to her divorce and to her taking her back, and she should not do it again. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata’ used to say: And bring to witness two just men from among you meaning it is not permissible in marriage, divorce, or taking her back except by two just witnesses, as God the Almighty said, unless there is an excuse. And the Almighty said: This is an admonition to him who believes in God and the Last Day. That is, what We have commanded you to do of having witnesses and establishing testimony is only to be followed by one who believes in God and the Last Day, and that this is what He has prescribed for him and by one who fears the punishment of God in the Hereafter. From here, Al-Shafi’i went in one of his two opinions to the necessity of having witnesses in the case of taking back the wife, just as it is necessary in his opinion at the beginning of the marriage contract. A group of scholars have said this, and whoever said this says: Taking back the wife is not valid except by word so that witnesses are present for it. God the Almighty says: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect. That is, whoever fears God in what He has commanded him and leaves what He has forbidden - He will make for him a way out and will provide for him from where he does not expect, i.e., from a source that would never cross his mind. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Kahmas bin Al-Hasan told us, Abu Al-Sulayl told us, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) kept reciting to me this verse: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect. Until he finished the verse, then he said: O Abu Dharr, if all of the people took it, it would suffice them. He kept reciting it and repeating it to me until I fell asleep, then he said: O Abu Dharr, what will you do when you leave Madinah? I said: I will go to spaciousness and ease and be a dove among the doves of Makkah. He said: What will you do when you are expelled from Makkah? I said: I will go to spaciousness and ease, to Syria and the Holy Land. He said: And what will you do when you are expelled from Syria? I said: Then by He who sent you with the truth, I will place my sword on my shoulder. He said: Or something better than that? I said: Or something better than that? He said: You will hear and obey, even if he is an Abyssinian slave. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, Ya’la bin Ubaid told us, Zakariya told us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Masoud say: The most comprehensive verse in the Quran is Indeed, God commands justice and doing good. And the greatest verse in the Quran in terms of relief is: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. And in Al-Musnad: Mahdi bin Ja’far told me, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Mus’ab, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites Istighfar frequently, God will make for him a way out of every worry and a way out of every difficulty, and will provide for him from where he does not expect. Ali ibn Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out, meaning, He will save him from every distress in this world and the Hereafter, and will provide for him from where he does not expect. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham said, He will make for him a way out, meaning from everything that is difficult for people. Ikrimah said, Whoever divorces as God has commanded him, He will make for him a way out. This is also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Mas’ud and Masruq said, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out, knowing that God will give if He wills and withhold if He wills, from where he does not expect, meaning from where he does not know. Qatadah said, And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out, meaning from the doubts of matters and distress at death, and will provide for him from where he does not expect, from where he hopes or does not expect. Al-Suddi said: And whoever fears God is used according to the Sunnah and is referred to according to the Sunnah. He claimed that a man from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i had a son, and the polytheists captured him and he was among them. His father used to come to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and complain to him about his son’s situation, his condition, and his need. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to order him to be patient and say to him: God will make a way out for you. Shortly after that, his son escaped from the hands of the enemy. He passed by some of the enemy’s sheep, drove them away, and brought them to his father. He also brought with him wealth that he had acquired from the spoils. So this verse was revealed about him: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. It was also narrated via Salim ibn Abi al-Ja’d, with a similar chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Waki` told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Isa, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Thawban, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A servant is deprived of provision because of the sin he commits, and nothing averts fate except supplication, and nothing increases lifespan except righteousness. Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Sufyan, and he is also ath-Thawri. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Malik al-Ashja’i came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: My son Awf has been taken prisoner. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Send him a message, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, orders you to say often: ‘There is no power or strength except with God.’” They had tied him up with a rope, but the rope fell off him. He went out and saw their she-camel, so he mounted it and headed towards it. Then the people who had tied him up left him, and he shouted at them, following one after the other. He did not surprise his parents until he called out at the door. His father said: Awf, by the Lord of the Kaaba. His mother said: Woe to me! Awf was wondering how to present what he was in, so they raced to the door and the servant, and behold, Awf had filled the courtyard with camels. He told his father about him and the camels, but his father said: Stop until I go to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ask him about them. So he went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and told him about Awf and the camels, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Do with them as you like and as you would have done with your money. Then the verse was revealed: And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out * And will provide for him from where he does not expect. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us, Ibrahim bin Al-Ash’ath told us, Al-Fudayl bin Ayyad told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Al-Hasan, on the authority of Imran bin Husain, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever devotes himself to God, God will suffice him in every matter and provide for him from where he does not expect. But whoever devotes himself to the world, God will entrust him to it.” And the Almighty said: And whoever relies upon God - then He is sufficient for him. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Layth told us, Qais ibn al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Hanash al-San’ani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he told him that he rode behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one day, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “O boy, I will teach you some words: Mind your duty to God and He will mind your duty. Mind your duty to God and you will find Him in front of you. If you ask, then ask God. If you seek help, then seek help from God. And know that if the entire nation were to gather together to benefit you, they would not benefit you except with something God has already written for you. And if they were to gather together to harm you, they would not harm you except with something God has already written for you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.” At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Layth ibn Sa’d and Ibn Lahi’ah, and he said: Hasan Sahih. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ narrated to us, Bashir bin Salman narrated to us, on the authority of Sayyar Abi Al-Hakam, on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas’ud - who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever has a need and addresses it to people, it is a sin not to have his need fulfilled. But whoever addresses it to God, the Most High, God will give him immediate provision or a delayed death.” Then he narrated it on the authority of Abd Al-Razzaq, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Bashir, on the authority of Sayyar Abi Hamza, then he said: This is correct, and Sayyar Abi Al-Hakam did not narrate it on the authority of Tariq. And the statement of God, Indeed, God will accomplish His purpose, meaning He will carry out His decrees and rulings in His creation as He wants and desires. God has already set a [decreed] extent for everything, like His statement, the Most High, And everything with Him is by measure.

Ibn Abbas said: The longer of the two terms. I said, And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. Abu Hurairah said, "I was with my nephew - meaning Abu Salamah - and Ibn Abbas sent his slave Kurayb to Umm Salamah to ask her. Al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih, as did Muslim, Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah through various chains of transmission on her authority, as Muslim bin Al-Hajjaj said: Abu Al-Tahir told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, Ubayd God bin Abdullah bin Utbah told me that his father wrote to Umar bin Abdullah bin Al-Arqam Al-Zuhri ordering him to go to Subay’ah bint Al-Harith Al-Aslamiyah and ask her about her hadith and what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had said to her when she asked him for a fatwa. Umar bin Abdullah wrote back informing him that Subay’ah had told him that she had been married to Sa’d bin Khawlah, who had been among those who had witnessed Badr, and he died during the Farewell Pilgrimage while she was pregnant, and she had not long before given birth. She became pregnant after his death. When she recovered from her confinement, she adorned herself for the suitors. Abu Al-Sanabil bin Ba’kak came to her and said: Why do I see you adorned? Perhaps you are hoping for marriage. By God, you will not marry until four months and ten days have passed. He gave me a fatwa stating that I was permitted to marry when I gave birth and ordered me to get married if I wished. This is the wording of Muslim, and al-Bukhari narrated it in an abridged form. Then al-Bukhari said after narrating the first hadith at this verse: Abu Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu'man said: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us from Ayyub from Muhammad - he is Ibn Sirin - who said: I was in a circle in which Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla was present, and his companions used to venerate him. He mentioned the latter of the two terms, so I narrated the hadith of Subai'ah bint al-Harith from Abdullah ibn Utbah. He said: One of his companions whispered to me. Muhammad said: I became aware of him and said to him: I would be bold enough to lie about Abdullah while he is in the outskirts of Kufa. He felt ashamed and said: But his uncle did not say that. Then I met Abu 'Atiyyah Malik ibn 'Amir and asked him. He went to tell me the hadith of Subai'ah, so I said: Have you heard anything from Abdullah about it? He said: We were with Abdullah and he said: Do you impose strict punishment on her and do not make it easy for her? An-Nasa’i narrated it in his Tafsir on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la on the authority of Khalid ibn al-Harith on the authority of Ibn Awn on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, and he mentioned it. Ibn Jarir said: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abaan Al-Misri narrated to me, Saeed bin Abi Maryam narrated to us, Muhammad bin Jaafar narrated to us, Ibn Shabramah Al-Kufi narrated to me, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah bin Qais, that Abdullah bin Masoud said: Whoever wants, I may curse him. The verse, And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth was revealed only after the verse about the woman whose husband has died. He said: And when the woman whose husband has died gives birth, then she is permissible for her to be divorced. He meant by the verse about the woman whose husband has died, And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Saeed bin Abi Maryam with it. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad bin Mani’ narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ubaid narrated to us, Ismail bin Abi Khalid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: The last of the two terms was mentioned in the presence of Ibn Masoud, so he said, Whoever wants, I swear by God that this verse in An-Nisa’ was revealed after the four months and ten days. Then he said: The term of a pregnant woman is until she gives birth to what is in her womb. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Al-A’mash. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad told me, Muhammad bin Abi Bakr al-Muqaddami told me, Abdul Wahhab ath-Thaqafi told us, al-Muthanna told me, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, who said: I said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth - the woman who has been divorced three times or whose husband has died. He said: It applies to the woman who has been divorced three times or whose husband has died. This is a very strange hadith, rather it is rejected because in its chain of transmission is Muthanna bin al-Sabah, whose hadith is rejected once. However, Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with another chain of transmission, and he said: Muhammad bin Dawud al-Samnani told us, Amr bin Khalid - meaning al-Harrani - Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of Sa’id bin al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, that when this verse was revealed, he said to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him: I do not know whether it is general or ambiguous. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Which verse? He said: Their term is until they give birth - the woman who has died or the divorced woman? He said: Yes, and Ibn Jarir narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Musa ibn Dawud on the authority of Ibn Lahi'ah with it. Then he narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb also on the authority of Malik ibn Ismail on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah on the authority of Abdul Karim ibn Abi Al-Mukhariq that he narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth. He said: The term of every pregnant woman is until she gives birth to what is in her womb. This Abdul Karim is weak and did not meet Ubayy. And the statement of God interpretation of the meaning: And whoever fears God - He will make for him of his matter ease. That is, He will make his matter easy for him and make for him a quick relief and a speedy way out. Then God interpretation of the meaning: That is the command of God which He has sent down to you, that is, His ruling and His law which He has sent down to you through the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And whoever fears God - He will remove from him his misdeeds and make great for him his reward. That is, He will remove from him the forbidden and will give him a great reward for the little work.

65:6: God Almighty says, commanding His servants, if one of them divorces a woman, to house her in a house until her waiting period is over. He says: Lodge them where you live meaning with you according to your means. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and more than one said: It means your means. Qatada even said: If you cannot find anything except next to your house, then house her in it. God Almighty says: And do not harm them in order to oppress them Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It means he should oppress her so that she would ransom herself from him with her money or leave his house. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha: And do not harm them in order to oppress them meaning he should divorce her, and if two days remain he should take her back. God the Almighty said: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. Many scholars, including Ibn Abbas, a group of the early Muslims, and groups of the later Muslims, said: This applies to a woman who has been divorced irrevocably: if she is pregnant, then she must be spent on until she gives birth. They said, based on the evidence that her maintenance is obligatory in a revocable divorce, whether she is pregnant or not. Others said: Rather, the entire context is about revocable divorces, and the text only stipulates that maintenance is obligatory for the pregnant woman, even if she is a revocable divorce, because pregnancy usually lasts a long time, so it was necessary to stipulate that maintenance is obligatory until she gives birth, lest anyone think that maintenance is only obligatory for the duration of the waiting period. Then the scholars differed as to whether maintenance is due to the pregnancy or for the pregnancy alone? There are two opinions stated explicitly by Al-Shafi’i and others, and many issues branch off from them, mentioned in the science of branches. And the Almighty said: If they breastfeed for you, meaning if they give birth while they are divorced, then they have been divorced by the expiry of their waiting period, and she has the right to breastfeed the child or to refuse him, but only after nourishing him with colostrum, which is the first milk without which the newborn is usually unable to survive. If she breastfeeds, she is entitled to the wages of her peers, and she has the right to contract with his father or guardian for whatever wages they agree upon. For this reason, the Almighty said: If they breastfeed for you, give them their wages, and the Almighty said: And consult among yourselves in kindness, meaning: let your affairs be among you in kindness without causing harm or injury, as the Almighty said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Let not a mother be harmed by her child, nor a father by his child, and the Almighty said: And if you disagree, then another shall breastfeed for him, meaning if the man and woman disagree and the woman asks for a lot of wages for breastfeeding and the man does not respond to her, or the man gives a little and she does not agree to it, then let someone else breastfeed him. If the mother agrees to what a foreigner is hired for, then she is more deserving. With her son. God the Almighty said: Let one with an abundance spend from his abundance meaning let the father or guardian spend on the child according to his ability. “And whoever is restricted in his provision - let him spend from what God has given him. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.” Like His Almighty saying: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. Ibn Jarir narrated: Ibn Humayd told us, Hakam told us on the authority of Abu Sinan who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked about Abu Ubaydah and it was said that he wears coarse clothing and eats the coarseest food. So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the messenger: Look what he will do with them if he takes them? It was not long before he began to wear soft clothing and eat the finest food. The messenger came to him and informed him. So he said, may God have mercy on him, how to interpret this verse: “Let one with an abundance spend from his abundance. And whoever is restricted in his provision - let him spend from what God has given him.” Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said in his great dictionary: Hashim bin Mazid al-Tabarani told us, Muhammad bin Ismail bin Ayyash told us, my father told me, Damdam bin Zar’ah told me, on the authority of Shuraih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari, whose name was al-Harith, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There were three men, one of whom had ten dinars, so he gave one dinar in charity. Another had ten awqiyahs, so he gave one awqiyah in charity. The third had one hundred awqiyahs, so he gave ten awqiyahs in charity.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “They are equal in reward. Each one gave a tenth of his wealth in charity. God, the Most High, says: ‘Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance.’” This hadith is strange from this source. And the Almighty’s saying: God will grant, after hardship, ease is a promise from Him, and His promise is true and He does not break it. This is like His saying, the Almighty: “For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.” Imam Ahmad narrated a hadith that it is good to mention here. He said: Hashim bin Al-Qasim told us, Abdul Hamid bin Bahram told us, Shahr bin Hawshab told us, he said: Abu Hurairah said: While a man and a woman from the early Muslims were unable to do anything, the man came from his travels and entered upon his wife hungry, having been afflicted with severe famine. He said to his wife: Do you have anything? She said: Yes, be of good cheer. God’s provision has come to us. So he urged her, saying: Woe to you! Seek, if you have anything. She said: Yes. For a while, hoping for God’s mercy. Then, when the waiting period became long, he said: Woe to you! My people! Seek, if you have anything, and bring it to me, for I have reached the age of puberty and I have become tired. She said: Yes, now let us open the oven, do not be in a hurry. So, when he was silent for a while and she waited for him to say to her, she said to herself: If only I could get up and look into my oven. So she got up and looked at her oven, filled with sheep’s rumps and her two millstones were grinding. So she got up to the millstone, shook it, and took out what was in her oven of sheep’s rumps. He said in another place: Abu Amir told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Muhammad, who is Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man entered upon his family, and when he saw their poverty, he went out into the wilderness. When his wife saw this, she went to the millstone and put it down, and to the oven and lit it, then she said: O God, provide for us. She looked, and behold, the basin was full. He said: I went to the oven and found it full. He said: The husband returned and said: Did you get anything after I left? His wife said: Yes, from our Lord. So he went to the millstone and mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you had not lifted it, it would have continued to turn until the Day of Resurrection.
65:7: God Almighty says, commanding His servants, if one of them divorces a woman, to house her in a house until her waiting period is over. He says: Lodge them where you live meaning with you according to your means. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and more than one said: It means your means. Qatada even said: If you cannot find anything except next to your house, then house her in it. God Almighty says: And do not harm them in order to oppress them Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It means he should oppress her so that she would ransom herself from him with her money or leave his house. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha: And do not harm them in order to oppress them meaning he should divorce her, and if two days remain he should take her back. God the Almighty said: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. Many scholars, including Ibn Abbas, a group of the early Muslims, and groups of the later Muslims, said: This applies to a woman who has been divorced irrevocably: if she is pregnant, then she must be spent on until she gives birth. They said, based on the evidence that her maintenance is obligatory in a revocable divorce, whether she is pregnant or not. Others said: Rather, the entire context is about revocable divorces, and the text only stipulates that maintenance is obligatory for the pregnant woman, even if she is a revocable divorce, because pregnancy usually lasts a long time, so it was necessary to stipulate that maintenance is obligatory until she gives birth, lest anyone think that maintenance is only obligatory for the duration of the waiting period. Then the scholars differed as to whether maintenance is due to the pregnancy or for the pregnancy alone? There are two opinions stated explicitly by Al-Shafi’i and others, and many issues branch off from them, mentioned in the science of branches. And the Almighty said: If they breastfeed for you, meaning if they give birth while they are divorced, then they have been divorced by the expiry of their waiting period, and she has the right to breastfeed the child or to refuse him, but only after nourishing him with colostrum, which is the first milk without which the newborn is usually unable to survive. If she breastfeeds, she is entitled to the wages of her peers, and she has the right to contract with his father or guardian for whatever wages they agree upon. For this reason, the Almighty said: If they breastfeed for you, give them their wages, and the Almighty said: And consult among yourselves in kindness, meaning: let your affairs be among you in kindness without causing harm or injury, as the Almighty said in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Let not a mother be harmed by her child, nor a father by his child, and the Almighty said: And if you disagree, then another shall breastfeed for him, meaning if the man and woman disagree and the woman asks for a lot of wages for breastfeeding and the man does not respond to her, or the man gives a little and she does not agree to it, then let someone else breastfeed him. If the mother agrees to what a foreigner is hired for, then she is more deserving. With her son. God the Almighty said: Let one with an abundance spend from his abundance meaning let the father or guardian spend on the child according to his ability. “And whoever is restricted in his provision - let him spend from what God has given him. God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity.” Like His Almighty saying: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. 65:8: God Almighty says, threatening those who disobeyed His command, denied His messengers, and followed other than what He legislated, and informing us of what happened to previous nations because of that, so God Almighty said: And how many a city rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, meaning it rebelled, transgressed, and was arrogant about following God’s command and following His messengers, So We brought it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment, meaning a terrible, terrible punishment, so it tasted the evil consequences of its action, meaning the aftermath of its disobedience, and they regretted it when regret would not benefit them, “and the outcome of its action was loss. God has prepared for them a severe punishment,” meaning in the Hereafter, along with the punishment He hastened for them in this world. Then God Almighty said, after narrating the story of these people, So fear God, O you of understanding, meaning straight-minded people. Do not be like them, lest what befell them befall you, O you of understanding. Those who believed, meaning they believed in God and His messengers, God has sent down to you a reminder, meaning the Qur’an, as God Almighty says: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an and indeed, We will be its guardian. And the Almighty’s saying: A Messenger who recites to you the clear verses of God. Some of them said: A Messenger is in the accusative case as a substitute for inclusion and association because the Messenger is the one who conveyed the message. Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that the Messenger is a translation of the Reminder, meaning an explanation of it. For this reason, God the Almighty said: A Messenger who recites to you the clear verses of God meaning that they are clear, evident, and evident that He may bring forth those who have believed and done righteous deeds from darkness into the light like His saying: A Book which We have revealed to you, that you may bring forth mankind from darkness into the light and He the Almighty said: God is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them forth from darkness into the light meaning from the darkness of disbelief and ignorance to the light of faith and knowledge. God the Almighty called the revelation that He sent down light because of the guidance that is obtained through it, just as He called it spirit because of the life that is obtained through it in the hearts, so He the Almighty said: “And thus We have revealed to you a spirit by Our command. You did not know what the Scripture was, nor what faith was, but We have made it a light by which We guide whom We will of Our servants. And indeed, you are guiding to a straight path” and His saying the Almighty: “And whoever believes in God and does righteousness - He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. God has certainly been good to him in provision” An explanation of something like this has been presented more than once, so there is no need to repeat it. Here, thanks be to God.

65:12: The Almighty says, informing us of His perfect power and great authority, so that this may motivate us to glorify the straight religion that He has legislated: God is He who created seven heavens, as He says, informing us of Noah’s saying to his al-Nas 114:Have you not seen how God created seven heavens in layers? And He says: The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And He says: And of the earth the like of them, meaning seven also, as is proven in the two Sahihs: Whoever unjustly takes even a handbreadth of land, it will be hung around his neck from seven earths. And in Sahih al-Bukhari: He will be swallowed up by the seven earths. And its paths, wording, and attribution have been mentioned at the beginning of Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah when mentioning the creation of the earth, and praise and thanks be to God. Whoever interprets this as referring to seven regions has gone too far, gone too far, and contradicted the Qur’an and the Hadith without any basis. And in Surat al-Hadid, when God says: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, He mentioned the seven earths, the distance between them, and the density of each one of them being five hundred years. Thus Ibn Masoud and others said, and likewise in another hadith: “The seven heavens and what is in them and what is between them, and the seven earths and what is in them and what is between them, in relation to the Throne, are nothing but a ring thrown in a desert.” Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn Ali told us, Waki’ told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: Seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, he said: If I were to tell you its interpretation, you would disbelieve, and your disbelief is your denial of it. Ibn Humayd told us: Ya’qub ibn Abdullah ibn Sa’d Al-Qummi Al-Ash’ari told us, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Abi Al-Mughira Al-Khuza’i, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: A man said to Ibn Abbas: It is God who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, and the verse. Ibn Abbas said: What would reassure you that if I told you about it and you disbelieved? Ibn Jarir said: Amr ibn Ali and Muhammad ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ad-Duha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: It is God who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them, Amr said: He said: In every land there is the like of Abraham and similar to what is on the earth of creation. Ibn Al-Muthanna said in his hadith, In every heaven is Abraham. Al-Bayhaqi narrated this hadith in his book, The Names and Attributes, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a more detailed version. He said, “Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Ahmad Ibn Ya’qub informed us, Ubayd Ibn Ghannam Al-Nakha’i informed us, Ali Ibn Hakim informed us, Sharik informed us, on the authority of Ata’ Ibn Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, ‘God is He who created seven heavens and of the earth the like of them.’ He said, ‘Seven earths, in every earth a prophet like your prophet, and Adam like Adam, and Noah like Noah, and Abraham like Abraham, and Jesus like Jesus.’” Then Al-Bayhaqi narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah from Amr ibn Murrah from Abu Ad-Dahha from Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God the Almighty: God is He Who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof, he said: In each land there is something like Abraham, peace be upon him. Then Al-Bayhaqi said: The chain of transmission of this from Ibn Abbas is authentic, but it is somewhat anomalous. I do not know of anyone who corroborates Abu Ad-Dahha’s statement on this matter, and God knows best. Imam Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Ad-Dunya Al-Qurashi said in his book At-Tafakkur wa’l-I’tibar, Ishaq ibn Hatim Al-Madaini told me, Yahya ibn Sulayman told us, from Uthman ibn Abi Dahras, who said: It reached me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to his companions while they were silent and not speaking, and said: Why are you not speaking? They said: We are contemplating the creation of God the Almighty. He said: “Then do likewise, contemplate the creation of God and do not contemplate Him, for in this Maghrib there is a white land whose light is its courtyard—or he said its courtyard is its light—the distance of the sun for forty days. In it are creations of God the Almighty who never disobeyed God for the blink of an eye.” They said: Then where is the devil from them? He said: Do they know whether Satan was created or not? They said: From the children of Adam? He said: They do not know whether Adam was created or not? This is a mursal hadith and it is very objectionable. Uthman ibn Abi Dahras was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim in his book, and he said: It was narrated on the authority of a man from the family of Al-Hakam ibn Abi Al-Aas, and from him Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, Yahya ibn Salim At-Ta’ifi, and Ibn Al-Mubarak. I heard my father say that. The end of the interpretation of Surat At-Talaq, and praise and thanks be to God.
